raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The multi-layer EAGLE draft-extend CUDA graph (`--enable-multi-layer-eagle`) lays out each request's draft tokens plus its boundary-KV front rows (`speculative_num_steps - 1` plus the conv warmup rows; 4 + 5 = 9 rows per request for Inkling-Small at 3 steps) and stamps that width on `spec_info.num_tokens_per_req`. The Triton attention backend's captured draft extend ignored it: `_update_draft_extend_buffers` strided `qo_indptr` by `num_draft_tokens`, and the captured metadata took the same number as `max_extend_len`, so every request after the first was read at the wrong rows.

The output stays correct, because verification rejects the bad drafts, but the drafts degrade: with CUDA graphs on, an Inkling-Small MTP head on Triton accepts 1.51 tokens per step instead of about 2.92, on both the default and the unified-memory pool. With CUDA graphs off, and on the FlashAttention backends, the width is read from the batch and is right.

## Modifications

- New `TritonAttnBackend._draft_extend_num_tokens_per_req`: the stamped `spec_info.num_tokens_per_req` when it is set (positive), else the previous rule (`num_draft_tokens` for the V2 draft extend, `speculative_num_steps + 1` otherwise), as the target-verify width already does.
- `_update_draft_extend_buffers` (the `qo_indptr` filled before replay) and the captured draft-extend metadata (`max_extend_len`) both take the width from it.
- A graph replays only when the batch's stamped width equals its captured one, and the plain EAGLE draft-extend graph captures exactly `num_draft_tokens`, so nothing else changes.

Test (CPU), `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_triton_verify_metadata.py`: `test_graph_draft_extend_uses_the_runner_width` captures and replays a draft extend with a stamped width of 9 and `num_draft_tokens` 4, and checks `qo_indptr` and `max_extend_len`; unset widths (None, -1, 0) keep 4. On main the width-9 case fails (`qo_indptr` [0, 4, 8], expected [0, 9, 18]).

## Accuracy Tests

SM90, main `76d5b3ce02`, thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small, TP 8, `--attention-backend triton`, `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-draft-model-path thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small --enable-multi-layer-eagle --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`, radix cache, overlap scheduler. Median accept length from the scheduler logs; sgl-eval GSM8K, all 1314 test questions, `--temperature 0 --max-tokens 2048`. The unified-memory servers ran with `SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL=1`, so a read of a never-written pool row shows up as a wrong answer.

| CUDA graphs | pool | accept length, main | accept length, this PR | GSM8K, main | GSM8K, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| on | default | 1.51 | 2.92 | 0.9482 | 0.9513 |
| on | `--enable-unified-memory` | 1.51 | 2.92 | 0.9528 | 0.9513 |
| off | default | 2.91 | 2.91 | 0.9528 | 0.9513 |
| off | `--enable-unified-memory` | 2.91 | 2.92 | 0.9543 | 0.9513 |

Paired by question, every GSM8K difference in this table is within noise (p >= 0.21).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked separately: the change restores the accept length the graphs-off runs already reach.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -158,6 +158,35 @@ def test_graph_capture_and_padded_replay_use_bonus_token_width(
     _assert_verify_width(backend, batch_size)
 
 
+class _DraftExtendInput(SpecInput):
+    def __init__(self, num_tokens_per_req):
+        super().__init__(SpecInputType.EAGLE_DRAFT_EXTEND)
+        self.num_tokens_per_req = num_tokens_per_req
+        self.extend_seq_lens_tensor = None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("stamped_width", "width"), ((9, 9), (None, 4), (-1, 4), (0, 4))
+)
+def test_graph_draft_extend_uses_the_runner_width(stamped_width, width):
+    """BUG REGRESSION. A captured Triton draft extend strides by the width the
+    runner stamps on spec_info (draft tokens plus boundary-KV front rows), not by
+    num_draft_tokens; an unset width keeps num_draft_tokens."""
+    batch_size = 2
+    backend = _make_backend(batch_size)
+    backend.num_draft_tokens = 4
+    backend.speculative_num_steps = 3
+    spec_info = None if stamped_width is None else _DraftExtendInput(stamped_width)
+    expected = torch.arange(0, (batch_size + 1) * width, width, dtype=torch.int32)
+    for in_capture in (True, False):
+        forward_batch = _make_forward_batch(batch_size, spec_info)
+        forward_batch.forward_mode = ForwardMode.DRAFT_EXTEND_V2
+        backend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph(forward_batch, in_capture=in_capture)
+        assert torch.equal(backend.qo_indptr[: batch_size + 1], expected)
+        if in_capture:
+            assert backend.forward_metadata.max_extend_len == width
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("with_spec_info", (False, True))
 def test_unified_target_verify_uses_resolved_metadata(with_spec_info):
